# Copilot instructions: 93601V VEX V5 robot code

Team 93601V, VEX V5 Robotics Competition, game **Override** (2026-27).
Students own this code: explain changes in plain words and keep comments simple.
Nothing here has been tested on the robot unless a note says so.

## The current robot (tank drive)

- **`TankDrive.cpp`** (driver only) and **`TankComp.cpp`** (competition: brain-screen
  auton selector, odometry, six 15 s match autons, a 60 s skills auton, TEST routine).
- Ports: drive left 3 (front) + 11 (back), right 8 (front) + 20 (back, right side
  reversed); inertial 16; lift 1 + 10 (2 x 11W); side toggles left 2, right 9
  (5.5W motors); claw solenoid 3-wire A. The code headers are the source of truth.
- Drive geared 36:60 (motor:wheel). Drive, lift and toggles run on voltage
  (`spin(..., volt)`, 100% = 12 V via `VOLTS_PER_PERCENT`).
- Controls: left stick forward/back, right stick turn; L1/L2 lift; R1 claw;
  hold R2 = both side toggles spin, hold Up = they spin the other way.

## Other files

- Old code is on the `deprecated` branch, not `main`: `x-drive/` (the X-drive
  version of this robot) and `old-robot/` (the earlier robot).
- `HANDOFF.md`: how to switch computers, plus the dated "Where we're up to" log.
  Keep it updated. `scripts/sync.sh` matches .cpp/.v5cpp pairs, commits, pulls
  and pushes; `scripts/v5cpp_sync.py` only matches the pairs.
- Every program is stored twice: `Name.cpp` and `Name.v5cpp` (VEXcode V5 project,
  JSON with the code in `"textContent"`). **After editing a `.cpp`, the matching
  `.v5cpp` must get the same code**, or VEXcode downloads the old version. Run
  `python3 scripts/v5cpp_sync.py` to do that.

## VEXcode rules (these caused build errors before)

- Never add `brain Brain;` (VEXcode declares it). Keep the VEXcode Devices panel /
  `robotConfig` empty: every device is declared in the code.
- Use `Brain.Screen.printAt(x, y, true, "...")` with the `true` argument.
- Code is C++11 (`-std=gnu++11`) for the V5 SDK.
- The repo root is also a VEX VS Code project for TankComp: `src/main.cpp`
  defines `vex::brain Brain;` and then does `#include "../TankComp.cpp"`
  (VEXcode adds the brain itself, so it must never go in TankComp.cpp). The
  brain must stay above that #include in the same file: moving it to another
  .cpp makes the claw (`Brain.ThreeWirePort.A`) get created first and the brain
  crashes with a memory permission error.
  Edit `TankComp.cpp`, not `src/main.cpp`. `include/vex.h` declares
  `extern vex::brain Brain;`.
- Both tank programs were built with VEXcode's compiler on 26 Nov 2026 with no
  errors or warnings. If VS Code shows errors, it is usually the editor setup,
  not the code. `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json` is generated by the VEX extension
  on each computer (git-ignored); never write it by hand.

## How the auton drives (TankComp)

- `tankDrive()` is driver control only (voltage, uses `DRIVE_SIGN` and
  `TURN_SIGN`). Autons use `autonDrive()` (percent velocity, closed loop, uses
  only `DRIVE_SIGN` so turns are physically right whenever forward is).
- Heading is `fusedHeading`, updated in `updateOdometry()` from the inertial
  (times `IMU_SCALE`), or from the wheels using `TRACK_WIDTH` if the inertial is
  missing, unplugged or recalibrating. Always call `updateOdometry()` in loops.
- `driveTo()`/`turnTo()` use a sqrt stopping curve (`DRIVE_DECEL`, `TURN_DECEL`)
  and stop within `POS_TOL` / `HEAD_TOL`. `turnTo()` calls `wrongWayStop()`
  (ends the auton) if the robot turns 25 degrees the wrong way.
- The inertial is calibrated by `calibrateInertial()` at start-up and when CAL
  is tapped; all brain-screen drawing happens in the main loop (`showStatus()`);
  routines report through the `resultA` / `resultB` strings.
- Routines are written for red starting by the station, using `Spot` positions
  (`GOAL_A`, `WALL_N`, `{-35, -12}`...) that `onField()` mirrors for the other
  starts. Moves: `go(spot, speed, timeout)` drive and stop, `via(spot)` drive
  through, `face(dir, side)` turn a side (`CLAW_SIDE` / `TOGGLE_SIDE`) to a
  direction, `lineUp(target, fromDir, reach, side, speed, timeout)` stand off a
  target. Use these in routines rather than `driveTo()` / `turnTo()` directly.

## What has been done (newest first)

- **26 Nov 2026:** `TankComp.cpp` simplified (same behaviour, checked in the
  simulator): `Spot` positions, `go`/`via`/`face`/`lineUp` moves, one routine
  list, shared drive output, shorter header.
- **26 Nov 2026:** auton accuracy rework: closed-loop auton driving, stopping
  curves, inertial checks with wheel fallback, CAL button, wrong-way safety
  stop, CHECK ROBOT and TUNE routines. Simulated, not yet run on the robot.
- **26 Nov 2026:** side toggle speed lowered from 100% to 50% (`TOGGLE_SPEED` in
  `TankDrive.cpp` and `TankComp.cpp`); also slows the auton toggle flip. Old robot
  and X-drive code moved to the `deprecated` branch.
- **25 Nov 2026:** added `HANDOFF.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `scripts/sync.sh`,
  `scripts/v5cpp_sync.py` and `scripts/setup-mac.sh` for moving between computers.
- **24 Nov 2026:** tank drive moved to the ports above and to voltage control;
  auton minimum powers raised (`MIN_MOVE` 20, `MIN_TURN` 15).
- **19 Nov 2026:** robot changed from X-drive to a 44W tank drive; autons rewritten
  as turn-then-drive moves with encoder + inertial odometry.
- Earlier: Override autons written, side toggles replaced the single toggle motor,
  lift cut from 3 to 2 motors, 36:60 drive gearing added.
